model: KTA-302 BACnet MS/TP weather station gateway (Davis Vantage Pro2 / Vantage Vue)
applies_to: Ocean Controls KTA-302 gateways connecting a Davis Vantage Pro2 or Vantage Vue weather station (WeatherLink serial cable) to BACnet MS/TP.
summary: The KTA-302 reads a Davis Vantage Pro2 or Vantage Vue console over its serial WeatherLink cable and serves the data on BACnet MS/TP. 63 analog inputs cover barometer, inside/outside temperature and humidity, wind, rain, UV, solar, soil and leaf sensors, evapotranspiration and derived values; time and date objects give sunrise, sunset and storm start. Two configurable alarms (AV setpoint plus IV that picks the AI) drive two open-collector outputs reported as BVs.
notes: Time of Sunset/Sunrise are BACnet Time Value objects (instances 0 and 1) and Start date of current storm is a Date Value object (instance 0); the schema has no type code for them, so they are listed as Other, which makes "Other 0" appear twice.
AI units are writable to switch between imperial and metric (e.g. Deg F / Deg C, inHg / mmHg / mb, mph / mps / fps / kph, in / mm); the defaults are listed.
Names are kept as printed, including "Year Evapotranspitarion" and "Leaf Weatenesses"; AI 53 (10-minute gust direction) is printed with mph units.
AI Status_Flags alarm flag goes true when a Davis console alarm (set in WeatherLink or on the console) is reached.
The AVs carry a proprietary enumerated property 3306 that sets the alarm condition (0 equal, 1 greater than, 2 lower than, 3 Davis alarm flag).
Source copy: weathershop.co.za (retrieved via the Internet Archive).

source.title: KTA-302 BACnet MS/TP Weather Station Gateway

integration.summary: Set the MAC (DIP 1-6) and baud (DIP 7-8), connect the Davis console with the WeatherLink cable, then read the weather AIs you need. Units can be switched per object by writing Units. The two gateway alarms are optional: write the AI instance to the IV, the setpoint to the AV, set the condition and set the IV Out_Of_Service false.
setup: MS/TP master; MAC 0-63 from DIP switches 1-6 (binary); baud from DIP 7-8: 9600, 19200, 38400 or 76800 (the manual prints "78800"; 76800 is the standard MS/TP rate).
Device instance = 838000 + MAC; device name KTA-302.
The Ethernet port is not used for BACnet.
gotchas: Sunrise/sunset need longitude and latitude set in WeatherLink or on the console.
Alarms stay disabled until the matching IV's Out_Of_Service is written false.
